chapters.title: Engineering board
intro: This chapter is for agents who send product defects to engineering, and for engineers who fix them.
It explains the engineering board, escalating a ticket, linking tickets to work items, and releasing fixes.

sections.title: How engineering work connects to tickets
sections.intro: Some problems are product defects that only engineers can fix. You escalate such a ticket to engineering. SupportDesk then creates a work item and links it to the ticket.

list: A **work item** is a bug, feature or task for engineers. Each one has a key, such as `ENG-12`.
One work item can cover many tickets. All linked tickets follow the same fix.
A **release** is a product version, such as 8.1. You plan work items for a release.
When a release is published, linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

blocks: The **Engineering** board shows work items of the built-in tracker. Your administrator can also connect Azure DevOps or GitHub. Items from those trackers appear on the ticket, not on the board. Jira is not supported.

rows: **View the engineering board, work items and releases**
Open the **Engineering** board and the ticket's **Engineering** tab.
Escalate a ticket and link a ticket to an existing work item.
**Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases**
Create, edit and move work items. Add, publish and delete releases.

blocks.note: The board needs the built-in tracker. An administrator turns it on under **Administration** > **Engineering**.

sections.title: The engineering board at a glance
sections.intro: Select **Engineering** in the main menu. The board shows one column for each work item state.

blocks.caption: The engineering board with its filters, state columns and work item cards.
blocks.alt: Engineering board with numbered highlights on the filters, the New column, a card, the card menu, Releases and New work item

callouts: The filters: search, engineer, release and **Show closed**. The item count and the reload button are on the right.
A state column with its name, the number of cards and a short hint.
A work item card. It shows the key, title, priority, severity, fix version, linked tickets and assignee.
The card menu. Use it to move the card or open its details.
**Releases** opens the list of product versions.
**New work item** creates a work item without a ticket.

rows: Released or done. This column appears only when **Show closed** is on.

blocks.tip: The ticket badge on a card shows how many tickets are linked to it. A green fix version with a rocket means the version is released.

sections.title: Find work items on the board
sections.intro: Narrow the board to the items you care about.
prerequisites: You have the **View the engineering board, work items and releases** permission.
steps: Select **Engineering** in the main menu.
In the search box, enter part of a title, a key such as `ENG-12`, or a version. Press [[Enter]].
In the engineer list, choose an engineer, or choose **All engineers**.
In the release list, choose a release, or choose **All releases**.
To include finished items, turn on **Show closed**.
If **Load more** appears below the board, select it to see more cards.
sections.result: The board shows only the matching work items. The count next to the reload button shows how many there are.

sections.title: Move a work item to another state
sections.intro: Move a card when work starts, when the fix is ready, or when the item is done.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.
Drag the card to the new column.

steps.text: Or select the card menu (**...**), then choose the new state under **Move to**.
steps.caption: The card menu with the states you can move the card to.
steps.alt: Card menu with Move to New, Resolved, Closed and Open details

sections.result: The card moves to the new column. A message shows how many linked tickets were updated.

blocks.note: When a work item becomes **Resolved**, its linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

sections.title: Open and edit a work item
sections.intro: Change a work item's details, plan it for a release, or see its linked tickets.
prerequisites: To change a work item, you need the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.

steps.text: Select the title of a card. The work item panel opens.
steps.caption: The work item panel with its fields, repro steps and linked tickets.
steps.alt: Work item panel for ENG-2 with title, type, state, priority, severity, assignee, release, product, tags, description and linked tickets

steps: Change the fields you need. [Work item fields](#work-item-fields) lists them all.
To plan the fix, choose a version in **Release (fix version)**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Work item saved** appears, and the card shows the new details.

blocks.tip: Under **Linked tickets**, select a ticket number to open that ticket.

blocks.warning: **Delete** removes the work item for good. Select it only for items created by mistake.

sections.title: Create a work item without a ticket
sections.intro: Use this for engineering work that no customer has reported yet. To start from a ticket, [escalate the ticket](#escalate-ticket) instead.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.
Select **New work item**. An empty work item panel opens.
Enter the **Title**.
Choose the **Type**, **Priority** and, if needed, the **Severity**.
Fill in the other fields you need, such as **Assignee** and **Description / repro steps**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Work item created** appears. The new card appears in the **New** column.

sections.title: Work item fields
sections.intro: These fields appear in the work item panel. Fields marked optional on the screen can stay empty.

rows: A short description of the problem. Required.
How badly customers are affected: **Cosmetic**, **Minor**, **Major** or **Critical**.
The engineer who works on the item, or **Unassigned**.
The release that will ship the fix, or **Not planned**.
The product the item belongs to.
Optional planning labels that your engineering team uses.
How to reproduce the problem. An escalation fills this from the ticket.
The tickets that follow this work item. You cannot edit this list here.

sections.title: Escalate a ticket to engineering
sections.intro: Escalate a ticket when the customer's problem is a product defect. SupportDesk creates a work item and fills the repro steps from the ticket.
prerequisites: You have the **Create and link engineering work items** permission.
Your administrator has set up at least one engineering tracker.
steps: Open the ticket.

steps.note: On a narrow screen, the tabs are in a side panel. Select **Ticket details** (the sliders button) to open it.
steps.caption: The ticket's Engineering tab with one linked work item.
steps.alt: Ticket details panel on the Engineering tab with Escalate, Link existing and the linked work item ENG-2

steps: Select **Escalate**. The **Escalate to engineering** form opens.

steps.caption: The Escalate to engineering form. The repro steps are filled from the ticket.
steps.alt: Escalate to engineering form with type, priority, title, severity, repro steps, engineer, tags, the substatus check box, Cancel and Create work item

steps.text: Read the **Repro steps** and add anything the engineers need.
steps.note: Some trackers also ask for an **Area path** and an **Iteration path**.

steps: If you know who should fix it, choose the engineer in **Assign to engineer**.
To show the ticket as waiting for engineering, tick **Set the ticket substatus “Engineering”**.
Select **Create work item**.
sections.result: The work item appears on the ticket's **Engineering** tab and in the **New** column of the board.

blocks.note: The repro steps include the description, the customer's messages, analysis notes, product details and impact. Remove anything private before you create the item.
If the message **Ticket status unchanged** appears, the work item was created, but the ticket status could not change. Change the status yourself if needed.

sections.title: Link a ticket to an existing work item
sections.intro: If engineering already tracks the problem, link the ticket to that work item. Do not create a second item.
prerequisites: You have the **Create and link engineering work items** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **Engineering** tab.
Select **Link existing**.
In **Tracker**, choose the tracker that holds the work item.

steps.text: In **Work item id or URL**, enter the key or number, such as `ENG-12` or `1234`. You can also paste the item's web address.
steps.caption: The Link existing work item form with a work item key entered.
steps.alt: Link existing work item form with Tracker, Work item id or URL, the substatus check box, Cancel and Link

steps: Tick or clear **Set the ticket substatus “Engineering”**.
Select **Link**.
sections.result: The work item appears on the ticket's **Engineering** tab.

sections.title: Follow engineering work from a ticket
sections.intro: The ticket's **Engineering** tab lists every linked work item. Each entry shows the item's state and fix version.

rows: The item's state in the tracker, such as **Active** or **Resolved**.
The item is planned for that release.
The fix has shipped in that release.
The customer was told that the fix is released.
The item left the tracker. SupportDesk keeps the last known details.
SupportDesk could not get the latest state from the tracker.
Select it to see the other tickets that follow the same item.

blocks.heading: Actions on a linked work item

list: Select the key, such as **ENG-2**, to open the item on the board or in the external tracker.
Select the refresh button on the item to get its latest state. The refresh button at the top refreshes all items.
Select the external link button to open the item in Azure DevOps or GitHub.
Select the cross button to unlink the item. Confirm with **Unlink**. The timeline keeps a record of the link.

blocks.note: When a linked work item is resolved or released, the ticket gets an internal note, and its assignee is notified. If your administrator turned it on, the customer also gets a reply that the fix is released.

sections.title: Releases and fix versions
sections.intro: A release groups the work items that ship together. Select **Releases** on the board to see them.

blocks.caption: The Releases panel with the form for a new release and the list of releases.
blocks.alt: Releases panel with Version, Planned date, Product, Release notes, Add release, and releases 8.1 Planned and 8.0.1 Deployed

rows: The version is not out yet. The line shows how many items are still open.
The version is published. Its items carry the fix version.
The version is installed. The deployment date is recorded.

sections.title: Add a release
sections.intro: Add the next version before you plan work items for it.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
In **Version**, enter the version name, such as `8.1.0`.
Optionally, choose a **Planned date** and a **Product**.
Optionally, enter **Release notes**.
Select **Add release**.
sections.result: The message **Release added** appears. The release appears in the list with the status **Planned**.

blocks.tip: To change a planned release, select its pencil button, change the fields and select **Save release**. Select **Cancel edit** to stop without saving.

blocks.note: You can delete a release only when no work items are planned for it. Otherwise its bin button is unavailable.

sections.title: Publish a release
sections.intro: Publish a release when the version ships to customers.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
Find the release with the status **Planned**.
Select **Publish**. A message explains what happens next.
Select **Publish** again to confirm.
sections.result: The message **Release published** appears. The fix version is stamped on the release's work items, and resolved items are closed. Linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

blocks.warning: If your administrator turned on automatic customer notices, customers get a “fix released” reply at once. Check the release before you publish it.

sections.title: Mark a release as deployed
sections.intro: Record the date when a released version was installed.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
Find the released version.
Select **Mark deployed**.
Select **Mark deployed** again to confirm.
sections.result: The message **Deployment recorded** appears. The release shows the status **Deployed**.

troubleshooting.problem: The board says **The built-in tracker is not set up**.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace does not use the built-in engineering board yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to set it up under **Administration** > **Engineering**.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Engineering** menu item or the ticket's **Engineering** tab is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role does not include an engineering permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **View the engineering board, work items and releases** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot drag cards, and the card menu is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You can view the board but not change work items.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: The ticket's **Engineering** tab says that no engineering tracker is set up.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to connect Azure DevOps, GitHub or the built-in board.

troubleshooting.problem: A linked work item shows **Sync failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not reach the external tracker.
troubleshooting.fix: Select the refresh button on the item later. If it keeps failing, tell your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: The bin button of a release is unavailable.
troubleshooting.cause: Work items are still planned for that release.
troubleshooting.fix: Move those work items to another release, or set them to **Not planned**. Then delete the release.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **Could not move** a work item appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Someone else changed the work item at the same time.
troubleshooting.fix: The board reloads. Move the card again.

faq.q: Can one work item cover several tickets?
faq.a: Yes. Link each ticket to the same work item. All linked tickets get the updates when the item is resolved or released.

faq.q: Is the customer told when a fix ships?
faq.a: Only if your administrator turned on automatic notices. Then the customer gets a “fix released” reply when the release is published. The work item shows **Customer notified**.

faq.q: Can I link a ticket to a Jira issue?
faq.a: No. SupportDesk works with the built-in board, Azure DevOps and GitHub.

glossary.definition: A bug, feature or task for engineers, with a key such as ENG-12. Tickets link to work items to follow a fix.
A product version that ships a set of work items. It is Planned, Released or Deployed.
The release that will ship, or has shipped, the fix for a work item.
The steps that reproduce a problem. Engineers use them to see the defect for themselves.
Sending a ticket's product defect to engineers by creating a work item from the ticket.
